agentpcap observes the socket and pipe boundaries where language-model
agents reach their tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) carries every
tool call as JSON-RPC — over pipes for locally launched servers, over
TLS for remote ones. The tap reassembles those frames into MCP and A2A
sessions, classifies what it cannot bind, and appends every flow to a
lossless, per-host, append-only ledger.

One static Rust binary. No agent-side library. No routing change. No
gateway in the path.

## The three blind spots

1. **The path problem.** In-path gateways govern only what routes
   through them. Shadow deployments, local tools and off-network
   clients bypass them by construction.
2. **The decryption problem.** Network-side detection wants the
   encrypted payload. Without TLS termination on the inspection path,
   a tool call is unattributable metadata.
3. **The stdio problem.** The most common MCP transport never touches
   a network: JSON-RPC over the pipes between a client and its
   launched server. No network-resident product can reach it, ever.

One out-of-path instrument and one append-only ledger close all three.

## How it differs

| System | Covers | Limit | agentpcap's answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| agentgateway (Linux Foundation) | routing + policy for routed MCP/A2A traffic | in-path by configuration | the tap sees the bypass flows; exports feed one ledger |
| In-path enterprise brokers | MCP catalogs and enforcement at the enforcement point | coverage ends where routing ends | out-of-path capture on the host |
| SWG deep-packet inspection | MCP sessions under TLS decryption | decryption required; stdio invisible | opaque mode; the pipe collector |
| Generic eBPF observability | HTTP, DNS, databases, Kafka | no MCP/A2A semantics | protocol semantics as a first-class layer |
| AgentSight | eBPF capture at the system boundary; sub-3% overhead | agent-scoped, single host; no ledger | session reassembly plus the ledger as the product |
| Scanners | tool poisoning, rug pulls — at scan time | no wire-time record | capability drift at drift time from the ledger |

The one-line difference: the market answers the question each product
was built for. agentpcap produces the one artefact none of them produce —
the append-only, per-host record of who called what, with which
capabilities, when.

## Status

Early development, specification-first. The canonical specification is
[`docs/spec.md`](https://github.com/shsingh/agentpcap/blob/main/docs/spec.md)
and renders in CI. The implementation builds to it in Rust with eBPF
via aya; the evaluation fleet is the first milestone.
